project_overview.project_summary: This design production project centers on Typography-Focused Designer for VELLVÉ. The initial brief says: I'm looking for a typography-focused designer to help refine—not reinvent—the wordmark for my luxury longevity brand, Vellvé. Over the past several months, I've developed the creative direction through extensive exploration and mood boards. The work sits mainly in Graphic and editorial design, Design & Creative, Graphic, Editorial & Presentation Design. Stable project themes include visual concept and layout, brand and style consistency, production-ready exports. The available evidence includes 210 conversation messages, 1 deliverable files, which together document the brief, collaboration, review cycle, and delivered work. The recoverable artifacts span .png formats; their contents were used only where they supplied stable domain, production, architecture, or handoff information. For onboarding, the key task is to understand the intended audience, source assets, production workflow, review loop, delivery formats, and constraints that determine acceptance. No inspectable software repository was identified, so technical details are limited to what the brief, conversation, and artifacts explicitly establish.

business_constraints: Exploring subtle internal reveal lines or dimensional details that create depth without feeling ornamental.

If there's one thing I'd love to achieve, it's this: the opening V should eventually become recognizable enough to stand on its own as a long-term brand asset, without ever needing a separate icon or monogram.
My goal isn't simply to have beautiful typography—it's to create something that could only ever be VELLVÉ.
In several of the studies, I found that reducing those classical cues allowed the right arm to carry more of the letter's identity without feeling decorative.
I don't feel the need to introduce new concepts at this stage.
compatibility_constraints: A version with and without the "Wellness elevated." tagline I'll provide mood boards, reference images, and the current logo direction to build from.
